newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines expects power surplus with gas project.
newsitem.headline: Philippines expects power surplus with gas project.

text.p: The Philippine Department of Energy (DOE) said on Monday it expected a surplus of 450 megawatts (mw) by the year 2002 when the country's first gas-fired power plant is put on stream.

Energy Secretary Francisco Viray told reporters an internal study showed the cost of the surplus will total $320 million but this will be outweighed by the estimated $6.7 billion to 7.6 billion in revenues during the 20-year operation of the gas project.
The energy department has awarded the sale of the 3,000-mw of gas-fired capacity to the National Power Corp (Napocor) and the Manila Electric Co (Meralco).
Gas will be sourced from the Camago-Malampaya field, the country's first major gas find located offshore in Palawan, southwest of the Philippines.
Under the service contract system, the government has a 60 percent share of the net proceeds realised from the sale of indigenous oil or gas finds.

"While there will be cost to the excess capacity, you should look at the net benefit. There will be less dependence on imported fuel, an estimated foreign exchange savings of $5 billion to $5.5 billion during the 20-year period that the plant is in operation and the birth of a gas industry," Viray said.
The Philippines had been relying heavily on diesel or bunker-fired power facilities after it suffered a power crisis in 1992 that led to outages as long as 10 hours.
Viray said the government can either absorb the cost of the excess power through revenues from the gas project or sell the excess to power distributors.

Viray said the total investment for the gas project amounts to $5.5 billion. These include production and offshore pipeline costs of $3.35 billion, $470 million for an onshore pipeline and about $1.69 billion for the 3,000-mw power plants.
